messages:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding sample app crashed for a new sign-up when they hit a 401 during the first API call. Go SDK returned raw HTTP 401 body, JS SDK throws an `AuthError` with a different message. We should align shapes so sample apps can show consistent UX.

alex: Ugh, thanks for surfacing. Which sample app and which endpoint?

maya: `quickstart-node` calling /v1/chat.complete with bad creds. Stack trace: ```{
  status: 401,
  body: { error: 'invalid_token', message: 'token expired' }
}``` JS SDK threw `new AuthError('token expired')` while Go client returned an error stringified from the HTTP response.

ravi: I hit the same yesterday in `quickstart-go` — we show a raw error popup like "401: {error: invalid_token}" which confused product. This looks like both message clarity and typed exception parity issues.

ciara: Two angles: 1) SDK parity (typed exceptions across languages: AuthError, RateLimitError, RetryableError) and 2) message hygiene for onboarding (human-friendly copy + stable machine fields). We should propose a small stable JSON error envelope.

alex: Agree. Proposal sketch: always return structured error with keys `{ type, code, message, details? }` where `type` is machine-friendly (e.g., "auth_error"), `code` is HTTP-ish (401) and `message` short user copy. SDKs map that to typed exceptions with `.type` and `.code` fields.

ravi: Love that. Also include `hint` optional field for retry guidance (e.g., "refresh token and retry" or "contact support"). That helps sample apps show concrete CTA.

maya: Example payload: ```{
  type: "auth_error",
  code: 401,
  message: "Authentication failed: token expired.",
  hint: "Call /auth/refresh or ask user to re-login",
  request_id: "req_abc123"
}``` SDK behavior: JS -> throw new AuthError(message, {type,code,request_id}); Go -> return typed error struct with same fields.

ciara: Small UX note — keep `message` short and user-facing; avoid raw internals. Put diagnostics (stack, raw headers) separately under `metadata` for debugging only.

alex: Implementation concerns: back-compat for existing customers + hosted API returns. For hosted we can add header `X-Redwood-ErrProto: v1` and roll out gradually. SDKs can fall back to parsing the old body if header missing.

maya: For onboarding friction, we should patch the quickstart apps to detect both shapes for now and display the new friendly message if present. Patch PR ready?

ravi: I'll open a tiny PR for `quickstart-go` to normalize errors into a helper `NormalizeError(err)` which returns our envelope. Will include tests for both legacy and `v1` proto.

alex: I'll do the JS quickstart and the SDK mapping for `AuthError`/`RateLimitError`.

ciara: I'll draft a short spec doc (1-2 pages) with examples and rollout plan (header flag, SDK fallback, sample app patches). Also include telemetry: metric for percent of errors with new envelope.

errbot: deploy-bot: Note: canary deploy window open tomorrow 09:00-12:00 UTC. Tag your changes if you want them in the canary.

maya: Nice. Action items: ravi -> quickstart-go PR (ETA 48h), alex -> quickstart-js + SDK mapping (ETA 72h), ciara -> spec + telemetry plan (ETA 24h). I'll coordinate follow-ups and update onboarding checklist. 

alex: One tiny question: should `type` use snake_case or camelCase? I vote snake_case for consistency with HTTP-ish codes.

ravi: snake_case SGTM. Keeps things stable across languages.

ciara: OK. I'm adding `error_type` examples to the doc: `auth_error`, `rate_limit`, `invalid_input`, `internal`.

maya: Cool. If anyone hits blockers ping me. Also we should add a tiny note in the SDK changelog about the new error envelope mapping. :memo:

alex: Will do. :thumbsup:
